note: The Phase 0 / Phase 1 / Phase 5 exit criteria, transcribed from 09_TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE_AI_BRAIN_AND_DEPLOYMENT.md §12.2, §12.3 and §12.7. A row is `met` only when the named evidence executes and holds. A row that a person must sign, appoint or run outside this tree is `owner-blocked`, names the owner, and carries the unblock path — it is reported as a warning, never as a pass. Phase 0 criterion 5 (an accessibility CI job that fails on ARC-I1) and Phase 1 criterion 3 (a synthetic emission missing accessible_alternative fails CI with ARC-I1) are the same fixture and are recorded once as P0-5; the merge is explicit here so nothing is hidden.

rows.criterion: A signed approval record exists for Doc 1 v1.2 and for this document; checksums are recorded in the register and verifiable by re-hashing the rendered PDFs.
rows.reason: A signature is an act of a person, not of a build. The checksum register exists and re-hashes correctly, but no signed approval record exists in this tree.
rows.unblock: Founder & CEO signs Doc 1 v1.2 and 09; Governance records the signature block in the register; `node tools/checksums.mjs --verify` re-hashes both PDFs and the gate flips when the signed record is filed.

rows.criterion: Every ADR in §11 shows a named Owner and a recorded Status; none reads unassigned.
rows.note: The file check alone could not detect a MISSING owner, so it was not sufficient evidence for this criterion; the adr-governance gate was added and is now cited as well. The gate parses the index, requires every row to carry a recognised status and a non-placeholder owner, requires every owner's role to exist in the appointment register, and cross-checks each ADR record in this directory against its index row for status and owner. It found the index naming three different owners than the records themselves for ADR-0013 to ADR-0016, and an accountable role (Chief Systems Architect) with no row in the register at all.

rows.criterion: A baseline commit has passed CI with a clean secrets scan and a published SBOM and provenance attestation, verifiable by opening the CI run.
rows.reason: This repository has no remote, so no CI run exists to open. The local equivalents pass (secrets scan 0 findings, CycloneDX SBOM, signed-attestation workflow committed), but the criterion is written as a CI run URL and cannot be satisfied by a local command.
rows.unblock: Repository Owner creates the remote and pushes `main`; the CI workflow runs the gate suite and attestation job; the run URL is recorded against P0-3 and the row flips to met.

rows.criterion: The light theme token set is committed and its contrast ledger is attached, verifiable against Design System v1.0 §3.4.
An accessibility CI job exists that fails a build on an ARC-I1 violation, proven by an intentionally broken fixture and a red build.
rows.source: 09 §12.2 exit criterion 5 merged with 09 §12.3 exit criterion 3; AC-23

rows.criterion: Officer roles left open by U-11 and OQ-7 are filled by name, verifiable against the register.
rows.reason: Three roles are named in the approved architecture document and are recorded in docs/OFFICERS.md (Chief AI & Model Orchestrator: Marcus Thorne; Chief Inclusion & Accessibility Officer: Noni / Amara Diop; Chief Learning Scientist: Nelly / Dr. Elena Rostova). Chief Systems Architect, the accountable role named by ADR-0013 to ADR-0017, had no row in the register at all and now reads VACANT. The remaining eleven roles have no named person, and a build cannot invent an appointment.
rows.unblock: Founder & CEO appoints each vacant role in docs/OFFICERS.md; the gate re-reads the register and flips when no row reads VACANT.

rows.criterion: A learner can enrol via passkey, or via provisional identity plus guardian consent token; the path taken is recorded in the audit log.
rows.note: Implemented branch: the guardian-consent-token path. The criterion is a disjunction - "via passkey, OR via provisional identity plus guardian consent token". The passkey CEREMONY is deferred by Slice 0 decision D-05, because it needs a browser and an authenticator; the seam is fixed and refuses with a typed error, and the attempt is recorded in the enrolment audit log. The path actually taken is recorded in the enrolment audit log, which is what the criterion asks to be verifiable.

rows.criterion: A withdrawal of consent visibly locks the sharing surfaces and does not block core learning, asserted by a scripted test.
A learner-facing output that bypasses the Guardian is impossible: the coverage assertion reports 100 %.
The PWA renders the light theme by default with a verified contrast ledger.
rows.note: The gate computes the theme the document actually renders from the document and the token stylesheet, then checks that the rendered canvas is the light canvas and that <meta name="color-scheme"> and the manifest's theme_color and background_color all agree with it. Before this gate existed the row was proved only by the manifest and the contrast tool, neither of which proves what the page renders: the stylesheet's base :root block defined the DARK canvas and the light tokens were reachable only through an opt-in [data-theme="light"] attribute the document never set, so the page rendered dark with light browser form controls painted over it. The row was MISLABELLED as met and has now been repaired.

rows.criterion: Re-pointing the adapter registry to a second provider completes without any learner-path code change, verifiable by the diff of the re-pointing change.
The adapter conformance suite is green.
All five tiers are exercised in a documented failover test, including the §6.6 procedure end to end.
Core learning is never denied on credit exhaustion, and no learner-facing message mentions credits running out.
No API key is present in a client bundle, in the sandbox, or in logs, verifiable by the canary-token sweep.
The provider egress allowlist rejects an unknown field, proven by a negative test.
